title: His grandparents' common sense and wartime stories
summary: He grew up with all four grandparents, still consults them in his mind, and recalls his paternal grandfather's wartime hardships.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. I think so too you know. You know I grew up with my grandparents, all four of them. And they had a long life. So I was already an adult and still having four of them around. And there isn’t one single day that goes by without me thinking of my grandparents you know, and whenever I have to make a decision about something or I have a problem I try to daydream as they could be here and I could ask them what would you do, what do you think. And it seems to me sometimes I hear their voices you know.

And the most beautiful thing is that I still remember very clearly their common sense. This is people that, they had good common sense. These were people, a generation of people that could weigh, in reality, better than us. Maybe because they went through the war and they saw things that — I’m sorry I was — it was toward the end of one of my grandparents, the paternal grandfather that I asked him about wartime. And I never did before. And he told me things that I would have never imagined you know. Like being starving. Like walking in the snow without proper shoes for days, you know? And things like this. So these people, they had to have a better approach with reality. The coping mechanism with reality and being — developing good common sense, that with most of us is missing now.
